etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English continuen, from Old French continuer, from Latin continuāre. Displaced native Old English þurhwunian.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To proceed with (doing an activity); to prolong (an activity).

quote.text: Firstly, I continue to base most species treatments on personally collected material, rather than on herbarium plants.

quote.citation: 1905, E. M. Forster, Where Angels Fear to Tread , chapter 4:
quote.text: Gino was distracted. She knew why; he wanted a son. He could talk and think of nothing else. (video games) An option allowing the player to resume play after game over, when all lives have been lost, while retaining their progress.
